title: Sphere Packing in Dimension 7
content: We prove that the optimal sphere packing density in $\mathbb{R}^7$ equals $\pi^3/105$, achieved by the scaled root lattice $\sqrt{2}\,E_7$. The proof is local: every Voronoi cell of a unit-ball packing in $\mathbb{R}^7$ attains volume at least that of the $E_7$ Voronoi cell, with equality characterised by the local $E_7$ geometry. The Voronoi domain of $\sqrt{2}\,E_7$ decomposes into $115$ combinatorial chamber types under the Weyl group $W(E_7)$. For each chamber type we construct an explicit sum-of-squares certificate verifying positivity of the angular surplus $F_\Omega(\theta)$ on $(0,\pi/3]$, confirmed by exact rational $7\times 7$ $LDL^\top$ decomposition; all $115\times 7=805$ pivots are recorded positive, with tightest pivot $d_4^{F028}=2/7$. A uniform Taylor expansion gives $F_\Omega(\theta)=\tfrac{1}{3}\theta^2+O(\theta^3)$ near zero, and a global Lipschitz argument closes the range $[0.1,\pi/3]$. This resolves the seven-dimensional sphere packing problem.
